point: Western industrial society operates on the assumption that maximizing individual choice is the key to maximizing freedom and human welfare.
quote: the more choice people have the more freedom they have and the more freedom they have the more welfare they have

point: The dramatic explosion of choices across essential domains like healthcare shifts difficult decision-making burdens onto individuals.
quote: what it really is is a shifting of the burden and the responsibility for decision making from somebody who knows something

point: An overwhelming number of choices paradoxically leads to paralysis rather than personal liberation.
quote: one effect paradoxically is that it produces paralysis rather than liberation with so many options to choose from

point: Offering too many investment choices causes people to delay important financial decisions and miss out on valuable benefits.
quote: for every ten mutual funds the employer offered rate of participation went down two percent

point: Having numerous alternatives fosters regret, reducing the satisfaction we experience from the choices we make.
quote: this imagined alternative induces you to regret the decision you made and this regret subtracts from the satisfaction you get

point: Considering rejected alternatives incurs opportunity costs that detract from the enjoyment of our chosen option.
quote: opportunity costs subtract from the satisfaction we get out of what we choose even when what we choose is terrific

point: A surplus of options drastically escalates our expectations, making it almost impossible to be pleasantly surprised by the outcome.
quote: adding options to people's lives can't help but increase the expectations people have about how good those options will be

point: When numerous options exist, individuals blame themselves for imperfect outcomes, contributing to widespread depression.
quote: when people make decisions and even though though the results of the decisions are good they feel disappointed about them they blame themselves

point: Shifting resources and choices from affluent societies to option-poor societies would improve the well-being of everyone.
quote: income redistribution will make everyone better off not just poor people because of how all this excess choice plagues us

point: Establishing healthy boundaries is essential for human happiness because limitless possibilities create paralysis rather than freedom.
quote: if you shatter the fishbowl so that everything is possible you don't have freedom you have paralysis
